title: Geodesics, parallel transport and the exponential map
summary: Vector fields along curves and the covariant derivative D/dt (Proposition 7.2); parallel vector fields and geodesics (Definition 7.4); existence and uniqueness of parallel transport (Theorem 7.5) and of geodesics (Theorem 7.9); the geodesic equation in coordinates; the exponential map and normal neighbourhoods (Definition 7.21); geodesics as locally shortest paths (Theorem 7.23); geodesics of spheres and Lie groups.

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is Gudmundsson chapter 7 (Definitions 7.1, 7.4, 7.21; Proposition 7.2; Theorems 7.5, 7.9, 7.23; Examples 7.12–7.17) with Sternberg §3.3–3.4 and chapter 6 as open-licensed alternatives and Lee chapters 4–5 as the commercial reference.

preparation.description: Read Gudmundsson chapter 7, pp. 91–94: Definition 7.1 (vector fields along curves), Proposition 7.2 (the operator D/dt), Remark 7.3, Definition 7.4 (parallel fields, geodesics).
Read pp. 94–98: Theorem 7.5 (parallel transport), Theorem 7.9 (geodesics), Examples 7.12–7.17 (Euclidean space, surfaces, spheres, Lie groups).
Read pp. 100–102: Definition 7.21 (the exponential map set-up) and Theorem 7.23 (geodesics are locally shortest).
Open-licensed alternative: Sternberg §3.3 (parallel transport), §3.4 (geodesics) and chapter 6 §6.1–6.2 (exponential map, normal coordinates).
